subject: geography

moments.title: Humboldt sets sail
moments.who: Alexander von Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland
moments.body: 5 June 1799: Humboldt and the French botanist Bonpland leave La Coruña, Spain, on the Pizarro for the Americas. They carry 35 scientific instruments — barometers, thermometers, sextants, a chronometer, magnetic dip needles.
moments.takeaway: The expedition was self-funded — Humboldt's inheritance from his mother. Independence from royal patronage shaped what they were willing to study.

moments.title: Climbing Chimborazo
moments.body: 23 June 1802: the party reaches around 5,878 m on Chimborazo (Ecuador) — at the time, the highest altitude any European had reached. They observed how vegetation zones change with altitude, the basis of Humboldt's later 'plant geography'.

quote.attrib: Humboldt, in Tableaux de la nature, 1808

moments.takeaway: Humboldt's 'Naturgemalde' diagram (1807) showed Chimborazo as a cross-section of climate zones — the first time geography was visualised as integrated system.

moments.title: Kosmos
moments.body: Humboldt publishes his five-volume Kosmos — a 'physical description of the universe'. He attempts a unified view of nature drawing on his lifetime of observation. Charles Darwin called his earlier 'Personal Narrative' the book that 'stirred up in me a burning zeal'.
moments.takeaway: Kosmos sold widely and shaped 19th-century science. It also warned about human-induced environmental damage from Humboldt's Venezuela observations in 1800.

now.title: Humboldt rediscovered
now.body: Andrea Wulf's 'The Invention of Nature' (2015) restored Humboldt's standing in the English-speaking world. He invented isotherms (1817), described the Humboldt Current, and gave his name to over 1,300 species, places and features.
now.open_questions: Why did Humboldt fall out of the English-language canon while remaining central in Germany and Latin America? His German nationality during the world wars, the rise of disciplinary specialisation, and the eclipse of the polymath all contributed.

reflection: Geography as integrated science begins with Humboldt. The discipline's habit of crossing physical-human, weather-vegetation, observation-theory boundaries is his legacy — and what makes it distinctive among the sciences.
